title: AI Daily Brief - 2026-06-23
tags:
  - applied-ai
---

## Today in One Minute

- Florida State University reports measurable student success using Google's NotebookLM, with practical lessons for polytechnic teaching and learning.
- Claude Code is now usable directly in a browser, lowering the setup barrier for coding assistance on Windows 11 laptops.
- PaddlePaddle released PP-OCRv6 on Hugging Face, a 50-language OCR model family ranging from tiny (1.5M) to mid-size (34.5M) parameters, suitable for classroom OCR projects.

## What Happened

- Google published a case study on how FSU integrated NotebookLM into student workflows, using it for grounded summarisation, study guides, and audio overviews from students' own course materials.
- Towards Data Science published a walkthrough showing how to use Claude Code in a web browser, removing the need for terminal-heavy local installs and making AI-assisted coding more accessible to students.
- PaddleOCR's PP-OCRv6 was released on Hugging Face, covering 50 languages, with several model sizes so users can pick a small footprint for laptops or a larger model for accuracy.

## Why It Matters

- NotebookLM at FSU shows a concrete, source-grounded way to use AI for study without students drifting into generic chatbot answers, which fits RP's focus on authentic learning and academic integrity.
- Browser-based Claude Code means RP students who struggle with local environment setup (Python, Node, paths, permissions) can still practise AI-assisted coding from a managed Windows 11 laptop with a browser.
- PP-OCRv6 gives lecturers and students a free, multilingual OCR option they can actually run, useful for projects in business, IT, design, and applied AI modules that involve scanning receipts, forms, or multilingual documents.

## Try This Today

- Upload one week of your lecture notes and slides into NotebookLM and ask it to produce a study guide, a quiz, and an audio overview; check if the output is faithful to your source materials only.
- Open Claude Code in a browser and ask it to refactor a short Python script you already use in class; compare its suggestions with your own version and note any issues.
- Try PP-OCRv6 on a scanned bilingual document (for example English and Chinese, or Malay) and check accuracy on names, numbers, and punctuation against the original.
- Pick one student assignment and draft a short "AI use" statement: which tool, which step, what was verified by the student. This connects to the FSU NotebookLM story.

## Teaching Angle

- Run a 15-minute classroom demo of NotebookLM with a real RP module reading, then ask students to spot one thing it summarised well and one thing it missed or distorted.
- In a programming class, split students into pairs: one writes code unaided, one uses Claude Code in the browser. Discuss differences in speed, code quality, and understanding.
- For applied AI or business analytics modules, design a small group task where students use PP-OCRv6 to digitise printed forms, then clean the OCR output in Excel or Python, surfacing real-world data quality issues.
- Use the FSU story as a short discussion prompt: "What does responsible AI-assisted studying look like at RP?" Ask students to draft 3 rules they would follow.

## Links

- [NotebookLM is transforming student success at FSU](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/education/florida-state-university-notebooklm/)
- [How to Use Claude Code in Your Browser](https://towardsdatascience.com/how-to-use-claude-code-in-your-browser/)
- [PP-OCRv6 on Hugging Face: 50-Language OCR from 1.5M to 34.5M Parameters](https://huggingface.co/blog/PaddlePaddle/pp-ocrv6)
